sourceInformation.perspective: Raised top-down orthographic 3D, with optional overhead camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU with WebGL 2 fallback, Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, PeerJS 1.5.5, AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded toy city, thick ink silhouettes, midnight blue, mint, coral and butter yellow
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for suspension, wheels and power cells; procedural steering, particles and Rapier crash debris
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written 112 BPM synth funk, synthesized effects and engines, formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: 1–4-player AI Hub ghost sessions; standalone 2–4-player WebRTC ghost rooms with PeerJS signalling and same-origin BroadcastChannel transport; 2-player couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: One-command headless suite: complete 312-token campaign, Rapier contacts, standard controller emulation, two-pad and keyboard couch controls, phone multitouch, offline audio, real two-page WebRTC ghost races, and official AI Hub checks at 2/4 seats, 150 ms latency, jitter, loss, and host departure. Screenshots review TV and phone layouts.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research. Native model knowledge; required AI Hub integration contract and pinned dependency packages downloaded directly.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: Testing caught 4 game issues: corrupted inline JavaScript, a deferred menu-focus race, hidden text-field focus during gameplay, and a score-race clock that paused during shift transitions. All were fixed.
1 critical issue: the corrupted inline bundle prevented startup.
The full browser input flow, followed by the official AI Hub harness, caught integration and focus problems that pure simulation checks could not.
A headless WebGPU screenshot was blank despite a live renderer. WebGL fallback captures were useful for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js node materials made a consistent three-tone ink look practical across the whole procedural city.

The first bundle insertion misinterpreted $& in library strings; replacement callbacks fixed it. Menu focus also needed synchronous updates. Headless WebGPU captures required a WebGL fallback for visual review.

aiHub.name: Dodge Alley
aiHub.description: Sweep gold tokens around an ink-drawn midnight block, queue a turn through a narrow crossover, and dodge oncoming rivals. Survive three arcade shifts, team up on one couch, or chase scores against up to three online ghosts.
aiHub.controls: A/D or Left/Right: inward/outward; Space/Cross/R2: boost; S/Down/L2: brake; Esc/Options: pause. Touch: swipe lanes, hold right side to boost.
